notCovered.tomes: A tome has no standalone output; its number is a DELTA against a reference build, and choosing that reference is a design decision this lane was not scoped to make. Named follow-on lane.
notCovered.relics: Relics span direct stats, economy, survival, movement and event effects. No universal reference build or grade was selected.
notCovered.characters: Confounded by innate + signature + starting weapon at once; not separable on this rig.
notCovered.coreWeapons: Campaign cores are aimed/manual-control weapons with a separate runtime registry. This automatic WeaponSystem orbit cannot measure human aim.

loadoutContract.orderLimit: WeaponSystem insertion order can affect cast interleave. Every controlled pair/build uses lexicographic weapon-id order; acquisition-order permutations are not measured.
loadoutContract.unlockPolicy: The laboratory roster assumes canonical unlocks are earned. Every measured build publishes its exact fresh-start/achievement requirements.

executionContract.note: Worker count changes wall-clock execution only. The CLI disables V8 Maglev before simulation, fixture workers inherit that process policy, and seeded tasks return in canonical order; numeric evidence and fingerprint are worker-count invariant.

axes.what: kills per minute against 72 respawning 35-HP enemies that pressure an orbiting player

axes.job: damaging a stationary controlled boss-class target
axes.what: damage per minute into one stationary 1e9-HP target

metric.whyTwo: Collapsing crowd-clear and boss damage into one score needs a weight, and a weight is an opinion. Two letters is the honest publication.
metric.whyNotSurvival: Survival is the metric a run cares about and it is NOT reachable per weapon: src/dev/headlessSim.ts has no per-weapon damage attribution (damageByWeapon is keyed by source phase), no starting-weapon override, and its draft puts four weapons in the run within minutes. Locking the others out does not isolate either, because partitionLockedOut falls back to the held ids when a pool empties. Reported as a correct negative rather than faked.

builds.note: Measured controlled-sim pairs and greedy candidate loadouts use their own published seeded cohort. They are laboratory evidence, not live-play recommendations.

heldConstant: player stats: neutral (might 1, attackSpeed 1, area 1, cooldown 1, critChance 0) - no tome, relic, shrine or shop rank
terrain: flat, no cliffs, no surfaces
player path: a scripted deterministic orbit, identical for every weapon
enemy population: fixed count, fixed HP, fixed spawn geometry, deterministic drift
timestep: fixed 1/60, no wall clock reads anywhere in the loop
weapon rarity bonus levels: 0 (common-equivalent authored level only)
limits: This ranks bare automatic WeaponSystem weapons, not aimed core weapons and not full-run builds. A weapon that scales with stats is measured without those stats.
The rig is WeaponSystem + Projectiles + GroundPatches. No director, elites, boss attacks/phases, player damage, survival, XP or draft economy.
The trash fixture respawns on death, so kills/min measures throughput and is not capped by a finite population.

The boss-class fixture is stationary and stands 5.1-7.9m from the orbiting player. It does not execute authored boss movement, attacks, or phases; this is target-damage evidence, not boss-fight performance.
A weapon whose reach is shorter than the controlled target distance measures ZERO there, and that zero is a fact about this fixture as much as about the weapon.
Echo's wake does not intersect the stationary boss-class fixture. Those bossDamage rows are explicitly UNMEASURED and receive no tier or rank.
Order statistics are discrete, never interpolated: quantiles use the nearest zero-based sample index round((n - 1) * q), and even-sized medians use the upper middle sample.
Measured controlled-sim builds are greedy four-weapon chains, not exhaustive optima or live-play recommendations.
Greedy build selection and reported build performance use the same deterministic seed cohort; there is no holdout cohort, so selection bias is possible.
Multi-weapon rows use a fixed lexicographic insertion order. Other acquisition orders are not measured and can change cast interleave.

tierLadder.rule: DERIVED per cohort (same form, same level). unit = median |ln(value / cohortMedian)| over the cohort; tier(v) = first z with ln(v/cohortMedian) >= z * unit.
tierLadder.whyDerived: A fixed ratio ladder was tried first and measurement killed it: this roster spans ~50x on crowd clear, so a fixed 1.6x S-threshold put 11 of 25 base weapons in S spanning 1.6x to 10.1x. True, and useless.
tierLadder.property: The floor is what stops the ladder manufacturing a tier. A roster flatter than ln(1.15) falls entirely inside the floor and comes out all-B. A percentile-bucket ladder always produces S-tiers whether or not anything deserves one.
tierLadder.perCohort: cohorts[<cohort>][<axis>] carries the dispersion this cohort derived, whether the floor bound it, and the exact multiple of the median each letter required.
